metadata.title: AutoStore Holdings Ltd (FRA:1IG) (Q2 2026) Earnings Call Highlights: Record Revenue and Amazon ...

content.text:
This article first appeared on GuruFocus.
-
Revenue: Record revenue of $192 million in Q2 2026, up 43% year over year and 16% sequentially.
-
Order Intake: Record order intake of $218 million in Q2 2026.
-
Gross Margin: Strong gross margin of 72%.
-
Adjusted EBITDA Margin: 45%, up sequentially from 44% in Q1.
-
Cash Conversion: 84%.
-
Order Backlog: $596 million at the end of the quarter.
-
Net Debt: Reduced by $46 million during the quarter, ending at $90 million, corresponding to a net debt ratio of 0.3 times.
-
Liquidity: $104 million in cash and a fully available revolving credit facility of $350 million, providing total liquidity of $454 million.
-
Full-Year Revenue Guidance: Around $700 million.
-
Share Buyback Program: Announced a program of up to $75 million, planned to complete over the course of the year.
Release Date: August 13, 2026
For the complete transcript of the earnings call, please refer to the full earnings call transcript.
Positive Points
-
Record Q2 revenue of $192 million and record order intake of $218 million, with strong 43% year-over-year revenue growth.
-
Continued strong profitability with gross margin of 72% and adjusted EBITDA margin of 45%, demonstrating business model scalability.
-
Announced a global framework agreement with Amazon, a significant strategic milestone that could expand future revenue opportunities.
-
Launched a $75 million share buyback program, reflecting confidence in the company's long-term prospects and cash generation.
-
Strong order backlog of $596 million provides good visibility into future revenues, supporting the full-year revenue guidance of around $700 million.
Negative Points
-
Full-year revenue guidance of around $700 million implies a slowdown in H2, with revenue expected to be roughly flat versus H1, despite strong order intake.
-
Margins are expected to slightly moderate in the second half due to increased investments in product innovation, software, AI, and commercial capabilities.
-
North America revenue was slightly down in Q2, despite strong demand in the region, indicating potential regional volatility.
-
The Amazon agreement includes no purchasing commitments, and management declined to provide details, leaving uncertainty about its near-term financial impact.
-
Gross margin slightly moderated from Q1, and while expected to remain strong, it faces potential pressure from input cost volatility, such as aluminum prices.
Q & A Highlights
Q: Can you provide more details on the agreement with Amazon, including whether it covers new or existing projects, the products involved, the timeframe, and any minimum purchase commitments? A: Mats Vikse (CEO): This agreement establishes a global framework under which Amazon can purchase our products and solutions. It does not contain any purchasing commitments at this time. We cannot comment on the details of the agreement or individual customers, as is our practice.
Q: The full-year revenue guidance of around $700 million implies H2 revenue will be roughly flat versus H1. Does this suggest that recent strong order intake includes more high-throughput projects with longer lead times? A: Paul Harrison (CFO): We are pleased to provide guidance today. The guidance reflects a very strong H1 performance and our prudent approach given the project-based nature of the business. It is important to note that the $700 million guidance still implies approximately 30% year-over-year growth, which would represent a very strong year.
Q: Can you quantify how much margins are expected to moderate in the second half due to increased investments? A: Paul Harrison (CFO): The moderation will be slight and reflects our decision to invest further in growth opportunities. We are very proud of the high margins our business delivers and will sustain them. You can continue to expect strong margins in the second half, and we still expect the gross margin to start with a seven for the full year.
Q: Can you provide more color on the drivers behind the record order intake, including geographic and industry mix, and whether Amazon is included? A: Paul Harrison (CFO): The order profile reflects the traditional spread of our business. Order momentum is strong in North America, and the standard segment was very strong, with a good contribution from high-throughput projects. There were no particularly unique orders driving the number. New product innovations like AutoCase and FlexBins are unlocking opportunities and playing a part in driving order momentum.
Q: Should Amazon be viewed not only as a customer but also as a partner, and will they have the opportunity to offer AutoStore solutions outside their own usage? A: Mats Vikse (CEO): The agreement provides a framework for how Amazon purchases our products, but we are not disclosing the details of how it is set up. We do have similar agreements with other customers. We see a trend of customers taking greater ownership of their automation as it becomes more strategically important.
Q: Can you provide an update on the level of recurring revenues in the business? A: Paul Harrison (CFO): Even in a quarter with very strong revenues led by traditional CapEx-based business, recurring revenues remain a double-digit proportion of our revenue base. This includes contributions from AutoStore-as-a-Service and software, which remain an important and strong part of the business.
Q: Are there specific features or functionality in the development pipeline that are bespoke to Amazon? A: Mats Vikse (CEO): We are a product-driven business and take pride in our standardization. We do not comment on individual customers or the specific features that may be developed for them.
Q: Can you provide more color on the phasing of revenue for the rest of the year, as a weaker H2 goes against typical seasonality? A: Paul Harrison (CFO): H1 was a very strong period with a number of projects secured for revenue. Given there is still a long way to go in 2026 and the strong performance, we are being prudent with our guidance of around $700 million. This still implies 30% growth year-over-year, which would be a very strong result.
Q: Can you provide an update on the AutoStore-as-a-Service business in Q2? A: Paul Harrison (CFO): We signed a couple of deals in Europe with a total contract value of around $8 million. This offering continues to play an important role in generating customer interest, some of which translates into traditional CapEx-based business.
Q: Can you separate how much of the recent growth is related to new product launches versus other factors, and can you put a number on the return from these investments? A: Mats Vikse (CEO): A meaningful portion of recent orders has been enabled by new product releases, which allow us to solve different use cases and sell our full suite of products. Investments in software like CubeVerse and AutoStore Intelligence provide customers with a system that constantly improves, with value compounding with every new robot deployed. This creates new opportunities and builds long-term confidence in us as the right partner.
For the complete transcript of the earnings call, please refer to the full earnings call transcript.
